papers.title: Algorithms for determining deadlines and COLREG-compliant manoeuvres for safe navigation in multi-ship scenarios using velocity areas
papers.title_zh: 多船会遇的决策期限与COLREG合规操纵
papers.boundary_note: 出版社仅给2026-10-26日精度，无法证明在线时刻晚于本期窗口起点2026-10-26 08:00 Asia/Singapore；作为边界日新增收录，上一期未见。
papers.version_status: version of record; open-access First View
papers.correction_status: Cambridge article page checked 2026-11-02; this review scope found no separate correction or retraction notice
papers.reading_scope: full_html_sections: abstract, introduction, Sections 2-9, equations/pseudocode, Tables 1/3-7 descriptions, Figures 4-15 descriptions, conclusions, references; PDF not downloaded; code not run
papers.research_question: Can a multi-ship risk field be converted into an explicit deadline and a feasible speed-heading manoeuvre that is consistent with COLREGs?
papers.sample_clock_inclusion: Deterministic simulated scenarios with one own ship and multiple target ships; targets inside LRS enter analysis. Risk state is updated from instantaneous AIS-derived kinematics and forward constant-velocity calculations. No observed voyage sample, event window or train-test split.
papers.core_method: For each candidate own-ship speed-heading cell and target, mark CPA<CPASafe in a 3-D Boolean polar matrix; union across targets gives the forbidden surface and the free-cell share. A real-valued matrix scores CPA/TCPA, heading and speed changes, and COLREG constraints; the target-wise maximum is minimized subject to path-slope and waypoint-deviation rules.
evidence_anchors: Section 4 equations (3)-(4), free-area matrix and 13-minute example
Section 6 equation (5), target-wise maximum manoeuvre matrix
Sections 7-8 COLREG weighting and route-return state logic
Section 9 conclusion and simulation-only validation statement
papers.principal_results: In the worked three-target scenario, free area is 60% at the initial state and falls to 35.4% after 13 minutes under unchanged motion. The example manoeuvre surface selects H=-9 degrees and S=19 kn; a pre-alert variant selects H=-25 degrees and S=18 kn. These are scenario outputs, not population performance estimates.
papers.author_claim: The algorithms can identify risk-free sectors, estimate the remaining decision window and select COLREG-consistent manoeuvres suitable for watchkeeping support or future autonomous integration.
papers.independent_check: The paper closes an operational gap between encounter-risk representation and an explicit action surface, but effectiveness is demonstrated only on simulated ships with trial thresholds and weights. No real AIS replay, navigator study, nonlinear manoeuvring validation or collision outcome is reported.

papers.claim_boundary: Rule compliance in a discretized constant-velocity scenario is not evidence of collision reduction, navigator acceptance or robustness under wind, waves, sensor gaps and interacting manoeuvres.
papers.relation_to_user: Direct Q03 method neighbor. It supplies an auditable action layer for multi-ship encounter fields, but must be coupled to observed behavior and environmental constraints before use in extreme-weather traffic reorganization.
papers.minimum_check: Reimplement equations (3)-(5) for one published scenario; then replay one real dense AIS encounter with ship-specific manoeuvring limits and compare the chosen action against observed manoeuvres and a nonlinear simulator.

papers.title: RIST-Net: A risk-aware spatiotemporal interaction and risk-guided multi-scale trend decoding network for vessel trajectory prediction
papers.title_zh: 风险感知的多船轨迹预测
papers.version_status: publisher version of record in volume 367 Part 2; full text restricted
papers.correction_status: ScienceDirect record and DOI/title search checked 2026-11-02; no separate correction relation observed in this scope
papers.reading_scope: abstract_only: publisher title, highlights, extended abstract/contribution preview and bibliographic metadata; full methods/tables/supplement not read; code not run
papers.research_question: Does explicitly injecting pairwise encounter-risk history into both interaction aggregation and horizon-specific decoding improve multi-vessel trajectory prediction?
papers.sample_clock_inclusion: Three real AIS datasets from Tianjin Port, Shanghai and Danish waters; five repeated runs. Accessible material does not disclose observation/prediction horizons, dates, vessel counts, filtering, split clock or leakage controls.
papers.core_method: Node temporal encoders represent vessel motion; an edge temporal encoder combines pairwise relation features with historical risk sequences; graph attention adds an explicit risk bias. A risk-conditioned decoder divides the future horizon into short-, medium- and long-term branches, concatenates them, then applies a fusion GRU and correction head.
papers.principal_results: Against the strongest reported comparator for each metric/dataset, mean reductions are 4.73% MAE, 7.44% RMSE, 4.15% ADE, 5.01% FDE and 4.82% FD. The authors report larger average advantages in Extreme-risk scenes.
papers.author_claim: Explicit historical risk improves neighbor weighting and stage-specific long-horizon prediction in complex multi-vessel traffic.
papers.independent_check: The increment is more specific than proximity-only or implicit-attention interaction models, but accessible evidence does not reveal split independence, risk-label construction, baseline identities or absolute errors. Prediction accuracy is not collision-risk calibration or proof of actual avoidance intent.

papers.title: Data-driven Bayesian analysis of port-call bottlenecks and turnaround time at the ship–shore interface in crude oil tanker operations
papers.title_zh: 油轮港口周转的微时钟瓶颈
papers.version_status: publisher version of record in volume 367 Part 2; full text restricted
papers.correction_status: ScienceDirect and two author-institution records checked 2026-11-02; no separate correction relation observed in this scope
papers.reading_scope: abstract_only: publisher highlights/abstract plus Dokuz Eylül and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan University publication records; full methods/tables not read; code not run
papers.research_question: Which micro-intervals in a tanker port call dominate non-productive time, and how should they be prioritized for port-call coordination?
papers.sample_clock_inclusion: Five years of real crude-oil-carrier Statement of Facts covering onshore and offshore operations. Accessible material does not state exact years, call count, ports, vessel inclusion/exclusion, missing-event rules or holdout design.
papers.core_method: Operational event intervals from arrival/NOR through All Fast, cargo handling and sea-passage start are clustered, then modeled with a Tree Augmented Naive Bayes network. Mutual information and variance-of-beliefs are used to rank influence on total port stay. Exact discretization, graph constraints and validation details are unavailable at abstract level.
evidence_anchors: explicit statement that fuel-based EEOI/CII is not directly measured
papers.principal_results: NOR Tender-to-All Fast is the dominant bottleneck, contributing 32.2% mutual information with total port stay. Authors report that pre-berthing delay matters more for the analyzed carbon-intensity proxy than cargo-handling throughput.
papers.author_claim: A micro-sequence Bayesian analysis can identify the ship-shore bottlenecks that port, ship and charterer coordination should target.
papers.independent_check: This is a useful operational clock decomposition, but Statement of Facts measure event time rather than fuel or emissions. The paper explicitly distinguishes turnaround indicators from fuel-based EEOI/CII; therefore the result cannot be read as a measured emission reduction.

papers.title: Extending the numerical ship maneuvering models in irregular long-crested waves to low-speed applications
papers.title_zh: 不规则波中的低速船舶操纵
papers.version_status: publisher version of record; publisher marks open access under a Creative Commons license
papers.correction_status: ScienceDirect, TRID and two institutional records checked 2026-11-02; no separate correction relation observed in this scope
papers.reading_scope: abstract_only: publisher highlights/abstract, TRID bibliographic record and institutional metadata; full equations/tables/supplement not read; code not run
papers.research_question: Can a previously calibrated manoeuvring-in-waves model remain valid in the low-speed regime where storm avoidance, waiting or recovery operations reduce control authority?
papers.sample_clock_inclusion: KVLCC2 tanker model; turning-circle simulations in irregular long-crested seas and low-speed course-keeping across wave headings, including Sea State 6 validation. Accessible material does not give run counts, speed grid, wave spectra, record length or exclusion rules.
papers.core_method: A time-domain six-degree-of-freedom direct-superposition framework couples an MMG calm-water manoeuvring model with a blended nonlinear seakeeping model, then compares turning indices and low-speed course keeping with experiments.
papers.principal_results: Authors report that, after calm-water calibration, prediction accuracy remains consistent across speed regimes; low-speed course keeping in Sea State 6 and rudder response for obstacle avoidance agree with experimental evidence within the reported qualitative summary. Exact error values are not visible at abstract level.
papers.author_claim: The direct-superposition framework extends reliably to reduced-speed manoeuvring in irregular waves.
papers.independent_check: The study adds the low-speed/wave feasibility layer absent from kinematic AIS models, but one benchmark hull and inaccessible error tables limit transfer to heterogeneous merchant fleets and real typhoon manoeuvres.
